headline: Comp sales beat plan as margins widen and guidance is raised
summary_short: TJX's revenue rose 9.2% y/y to $14.32B in the quarter ended May 2, 2026, with comparable sales up 6% and diluted EPS of $1.19, up 29% y/y. Pretax profit margin expanded 1.7 points to 12.0%, and full-year guidance was raised across comp sales, margin, EPS, and buybacks.
summary_long: Net sales rose 9.2% y/y to $14.32B on 6% comparable-sales growth, led by HomeGoods (comp +9%, sales +11%) and TJX International (comp +4%, sales +13%). Gross margin expanded 180bp to 31.3% on higher merchandise margin, favorable inventory/fuel hedges, and expense leverage; pretax margin rose 170bp to 12.0%. Net income grew 28.6% to $1.332B and diluted EPS rose 29.3% to $1.19. TJX returned $1.1B to shareholders ($604M buybacks, $471M dividends) and ended the quarter with $5.58B cash (vs $4.255B a year ago). Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance: comp sales to 3-4%, pretax margin to 11.9-12.0%, diluted EPS to $5.08-$5.15, and buybacks to $2.75B-$3.0B, citing above-plan Q1 execution partly offset by an expected higher cost of fuel later in the year.

drivers.explanation: Comparable sales rose 6% led by HomeGoods (+9%) and TJX Canada (+7%), with all four divisions posting positive comps and higher customer transactions.
Margin gain driven by an increase in merchandise margin, a benefit from favorable inventory and fuel hedges, and expense leverage on sales.
Expense leverage on above-plan sales, favorable fuel hedges, and stronger-than-expected merchandise margin drove the 1.7-point margin gain.

Company raised full-year FY2027 guidance for comp sales, margin, EPS, and buybacks after a quarter that beat internal plan, while flagging a higher expected cost of fuel for the remainder of the year.
